rationale: Uhrig LK (2014), Ohio State doctoral thesis, full 223-page repository PDF, identity matched by title and OhioLINK accession osu1416961549. Study protocols OSU-06132 and OSU-07085 enrolled 112 post-surgical oral-cancer survivors. Exposure was lyophilized Rubus occidentalis Jewel-cultivar powder in oral troches/lollipops/suspension, not eaten whole frozen raspberry. Methods pp. 48-49 describe harvest at -20 C, 40-mesh powder and formulation; pp. 65-69 describe BFI, ISI and HNCI. BFI includes mood only as a fatigue-interference item; ISI distress/worry concerns insomnia, neither is a standalone anxiety/mood measure. Results pp. 107-112 show overall BFI reduction over time but no within-person trend and no treated-vs-untreated ISI difference; ISI sample means did not significantly differ and its overall 20-week change was a 7% decrease. HNCI is speech/eating/aesthetics/social/QOL, not anxiety. Full body supplies no endpoint matching anxiety; excluded for 0493 frozen-fruit/anxiety, although a preparation-mismatched human black-raspberry study.
